summary.impactRadius: Low - Changes are additive and backward compatible

changesApplied.changeMade: Added new HTTP POST route /acp/stream that accepts ndjson request body, creates AgentSideConnection with HTTP streams wrapped as stdio, and returns ndjson response stream
changesApplied.reason: Exposes ACP protocol over HTTP to enable TCP transport connections. Remote ACP servers can now be reached via HTTP POST instead of requiring docker exec stdio pipes.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: Low impact - new route added before catch-all proxy, does not affect existing REST API endpoints

technicalDetails.streamMapping: HTTP request body → ReadableStream → ndJsonStream input, ndJsonStream output → WritableStream → HTTP response body
technicalDetails.connectionLifecycle: Kept alive until client closes request stream

changesApplied.changeMade: Changed default port from 0 (random) to 3000, updated description to document network access
changesApplied.reason: Provides well-known port for TCP transport clients to connect to. Random port (0) prevented predictable network connections from remote hosts.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: Low impact - backward compatible (users can still override with --port 0), enables network discoverability

technicalDetails.behavior: If port 3000 is busy, command will fail - users must explicitly choose alternative port

changesApplied.changeMade: Replaced stub (throws error) with full HTTP-based implementation. Uses fetch() to POST ndjson to http://host:port/acp/stream, wraps request/response as stdin/stdout streams via TransformStream
changesApplied.reason: Implements the critical missing piece for tcp:// targets. Enables acp_delegate to connect to remote ACP servers over HTTP.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: Medium impact - unblocks all network-based delegation use cases. Adds AbortController for connection lifecycle management.

technicalDetails.requestBody: TransformStream writable → stdin (client writes to this)
technicalDetails.errorHandling: Throws on non-2xx response or missing body

flow: 5. Server creates AgentSideConnection with HTTP streams
6. ndJsonStream wraps stdin/stdout for ACP protocol
7. ACP protocol messages flow bidirectionally over HTTP
8. Remote agent executes, responses stream back

rippleEffects.consumerImpact: None - acp_delegate tool behavior unchanged from consumer perspective, just unblocks tcp:// targets

testingRequirements: Start ACP server with: opencode acp --port 3000
Test HTTP endpoint: curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/acp/stream -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' -d '{...initialize...}'
Test TCP transport: acp_delegate({ target: 'tcp://localhost:3000', prompt: 'echo test' })
Test Kubernetes: Deploy DevBob pod, kubectl port-forward, delegate from host
Test connection cleanup: Verify AbortController aborts on close()
Test error handling: Try invalid host, non-existent port, non-ACP endpoint
validationChecklist: ✅ HTTP server starts with --port 3000 by default
✅ POST /acp/stream route exists before catch-all proxy
✅ TCPTransport.connect() uses fetch() with streaming body
✅ Stream wrapping: request body → stdin, response body → stdout
⏳ Functional test: tcp://localhost:3000 connects and executes prompt
⏳ Kubernetes test: DevBob pod delegation via port-forward
⏳ Error handling test: Connection failures handled gracefully
